ActionCosts.title: ActionCosts
ActionCosts.description:
What one action costs and is expected to earn, in the mandate's currency.

`revenue_if_converted` and `margin_if_converted` describe the order the action hopes for:
revenue is what the customer pays before the offer, margin is gross margin before the offer.
Leave them `None` when unknown (see `check_action` for how that is treated).

`offer_cost` is what the action commits against the budget. A decide `Bid` carries the
*expected* offer cost (cost per redemption times the chance of redemption), which is right for
spend but far too small for the margin: a customer who converts redeems the offer, so the margin
of that order loses the full cost per redemption. `offer_cost_if_converted` is that full cost;
`None` means it equals `offer_cost`.

LoggedDecision.title: LoggedDecision
LoggedDecision.description:
One logged decision with its outcome. The options are "act" and "do nothing".

`act_probability` is the logging policy's chance of acting at all, for an ACT row whose policy
chose among several actions; without it an ACT row's own probability is taken as that chance
(one action to choose from). For a NOTHING row the chance of acting is `1 - probability`.
`q_act` / `q_nothing` are an optional reward model's predictions for this row, for DR.

margin_floor_pct.description: Expected margin after the offer's cost, as a share of revenue, must stay at or above this (0.2 = 20%)

approved_template_ids.title: Approved Template Ids

approved_offer_ids.title: Approved Offer Ids

cohort_exclusions.title: Cohort Exclusions
cohort_exclusions.description: A customer matching any one of these is never contacted

Mandate.title: Mandate
Mandate.description:
The hard limits on autonomous action for one business, one version at a time.

Everything except `signers` and `status` is the *body*: the part that is hashed and signed.
Changing any limit therefore needs a new version and new signatures; revoking or expiring a
mandate changes only its status and keeps old signatures checkable.

catalogue_version.title: Catalogue Version
catalogue_version.description: Pin a catalogue version; default the latest, if any

MandateDraft.title: MandateDraft
MandateDraft.description:
A new mandate, in the shape of the founder's example request.

Give the budget as `budget_ceiling_inr`, or as `budget_ceiling` (a number with `currency`, or
`{amount, currency}`). A bare number with no currency is refused rather than guessed: the same
500,000 is a very different ceiling in INR and in USD. Channels may be left out when a catalogue is published: they are then the
channels of the approved templates. The validity window defaults to 30 days from `now`.

MandateSignature.title: MandateSignature
MandateSignature.description:
One person's signature over one mandate body, in one role.

The signature covers the mandate's body hash together with the person, role, key and time (see
`autonomy.mandate.signing.signature_message`), so a signature cannot be moved to another
mandate, another version, another role or another person without failing verification.

QuietHours.title: QuietHours
QuietHours.description:
No message lands from `start` up to (not including) `end`, in the customer's local time.

The window may wrap midnight (21 -> 9 means 21:00-08:59); equal start and end means no quiet
hours. `timezone` is used only for a customer whose own zone is blank or not a valid IANA name.

SignRequest.title: SignRequest
SignRequest.description:
One signature. Either carry it (`signature` + `key_id` + `signed_at` + `algorithm`, made by
the signer over `signature_message`), or name a server-held key with `key_id` (or neither, to
use the custodial key registered to `signer_id`).
